stem: The first quartile (Q1) of a dataset is 30 and the third quartile (Q3) is 70. What is the quartile deviation?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 40 is the inter-quartile range (Q3 - Q1 = 70 - 30 = 40), not the quartile deviation. The student forgot to divide by 2.
50 is the median of Q1 and Q3, i.e. (Q1 + Q3)/2 = (30 + 70)/2 = 50. The student used the sum formula instead of the difference formula.
70 is simply Q3 itself. The student reported the upper quartile as the quartile deviation, confusing the two quantities.

explanation: Quartile deviation (also called semi-interquartile range) = (Q3 - Q1) / 2 = (70 - 30) / 2 = 20. The inter-quartile range is Q3 - Q1 = 40; dividing by 2 gives the quartile deviation.

explanation_sections.punchline: Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2; it is the semi-interquartile range, not the full IQR.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the formula: QD = (Q3 - Q1)/2. Map: Q1=30, Q3=70. Compute: Q3 - Q1 = 40, then divide by 2 to get QD = 20.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always halve the inter-quartile range to get the quartile deviation; IQR and QD are related by a factor of 2.
explanation_sections.timing: 30-40 seconds. Trap: stopping at IQR = 40 without halving.
